_note: Finished leather goods made by the leatherworker from the tanner's leather (Complaints/612): shoes, a draught animal's harness and a sword scabbard. Every mass, hour count and life has no source found and is an estimate, marked in each yield_basis.

shoes_pair.basis: per pair of stitched leather shoes
shoes_pair.yield_basis: A pair of hand-stitched leather shoes or boots uses a bit under a kilogram of finished leather for sole, upper and thongs (no source found; conf D), cut and sewn by a leatherworker in about twelve hours (Bespoky Shoes atelier, https://bespokyshoes.com/pages/atelier, opened: 'each pair takes 10-14 hours of handwork' from one shoemaker, a modern welted shoe; was 8 hours; Round 2: Beckett Simonon, How long does it take to make a pair of shoes, https://beckettsimonon.com/blogs/resources/how-long-does-it-take-to-make-a-pair-of-shoes, opened: 'over 12 hours of skilled labor' for a welted shoe (cutting 1, preparing 1, stitching 1, sole preparation 2, lasting 3, attaching soles 2, insoles 1, finishing 1), so 12 hours agrees with two modern workshops; the leather mass is still without a source, so conf D). Thread and nails are a few grams and are left out. CLOTHING: the pair satisfies the clothing need at the factor leather_kg already carries per kilogram of leather it holds (data/world/needs.json), so a worked pair is worth its leather and no more until a source gives cover and warmth of footwear separately; a labelled placeholder, retire with a need for footwear.

harness_set.basis: per set of leather harness for one draught animal: collar pad, traces, reins, girth and straps
harness_set.yield_basis: Straps, traces and reins for one animal run to some eight kilograms of heavy leather and a thirty-hour stitching job for a saddler (author's estimate from the size of the pieces, conf D; Round 2, opened with no weight or hours found: Small Farmer's Journal Work Horse and Mule Harness Design and Function Part 1 (https://smallfarmersjournal.com/work-horse-mule-harness-design-function-part-1/), leatherworker.net forum thread on making horse harness (a saddler there says a single 6 foot trace has 4 rows of stitching at 8 a inch, 2300 stitches, and hand-making takes 'a huge ammount of time'), and Fitz-Gerald, The Harness Makers' Illustrated Manual (Project Gutenberg 78603; leather 'from six to twenty pounds a side', no set weight); metal fittings and the wooden collar or yoke are left out). It is a capital good of a draught animal: it is bought by whoever works the animal, so it has no household need of its own.

scabbard_leather.basis: per leather-covered scabbard and belt for one sword or dagger
scabbard_leather.yield_basis: A leather sheath with its belt uses some four tenths of a kilogram of leather and a few hours of cutting, wetting, moulding and stitching (author's estimate, conf D). It is the soldier's kit, bought by whoever arms a soldier, and carries no household need of its own.
